result:
Root cause and fix are in place, and the RCA task is checkpointed as `pending_review`.

**Root cause:** task-20260726-171926's own AI session actually succeeded (opened PR #578). The false "stalled" watchdog signal came from `/opt/veridian/scripts/worker-entrypoint.sh` (a live, git-untracked ops script) killing its periodic-checkpoint heartbeat right after the main `claude -p` invocation returns — before the unbounded quality-gate/auto-fix loop that follows. Any gate phase running past the watchdog's 20-minute stall threshold produces a frozen last checkpoint that gets misread as a stall, even when the system (preflight-guard's `memory_low` transient handling + systemd restart) is already self-healing, which I confirmed live: invocation 2 correctly rejected on real memory contention from concurrent workers, and invocation 3 was already running cleanly by the time I investigated.

**Fix:** removed the premature `kill/wait` of the heartbeat PID in `worker-entrypoint.sh`, relying on the existing `EXIT` trap to reap it — so `last_checkpoint_at` now stays fresh through quality-gate/auto-fix too. Verified with `bash -n` and the existing `worker_noop_pending_review_test.sh` regression test (still passes).

**known_fixes:** registered `signature="periodic checkpoint", fix_action="restart_unit"` via `superboss-register.py log-fix`; confirmed row in `superboss-register.sqlite` (success_count now 5, reflecting concurrent RCA activity on the same signature from sibling tasks — expected upsert behavior, not a conflict).

Note: while working, I noticed `/opt/veridian/scripts/quality-gate.sh` was independently patched by another concurrent RCA task (task-20260726-180000) for a related OOM root cause on a sibling task — complementary to this fix, not conflicting.
